page: Amazon Web Services r6idn.32xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by the Intel Xeon 8375C processor. This x86_64 architecture server features 128 virtual CPUs across 64 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a clock speed of 3.5 GHz. The system is equipped with 1024.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, the instance includes 7600 GB of NVMe SSD instance store volumes. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 200 Gbps, managed via the AWS Nitro hypervisor.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong multi-core and memory performance. The server achieved a multi-core stress-ng CPU score of 123839.46 and a Passmark CPU score of 86426.81, placing it in the top tier for raw computational capacity. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with read-only small block cached speeds reaching 6621.1 GB/sec and large block uncached read speeds at 331.59 GB/sec. Cryptographic operations perform exceptionally well, as evidenced by a Passmark CPU encryption score of 110416.81.

With its high memory-to-vCPU ratio and fast local NVMe storage, this instance is designed for memory-intensive and data-heavy workloads. It demonstrates strong capabilities in database operations, achieving 108.32 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and a Passmark database score of 29718.21. These characteristics make it highly suitable for large-scale in-memory databases, data warehousing, real-time analytics, and high-throughput web serving. The hardware profile offers qualitative cost efficiency by consolidating massive memory arrays and high-speed local storage on a single dedicated node, reducing the need for distributed clustering.
